newsitem.title: USA: Iraq's Hamdoon sees no hiccups on oil sale renewal.
newsitem.headline: Iraq's Hamdoon sees no hiccups on oil sale renewal.

text.p: Iraqi Ambassador Nizar Hamdoon said Wednesday that he foresees no political wrangling over setting in motion the renewed "oil-for-food" deal with the United Nations.
Instead, Hamdoon said Iraq was simply following procedures that a new aid distribution plan be in place before oil sales can restart.
"Until a distribution plan is agreed between us and the Secretariat, there can be no oil sales. This is normal procedure," Hamdoon told Reuters.

The distribution plan -- which spells out the content and logistics of delivering food and medicine imports to ordinary Iraqis -- is expected to be finalized by the end of June, an official with the U.N. Department of Humanitarian Affairs said Wednesday.

At issue is the scheme which allows Iraq to sell $2 billion worth of crude oil over 180 days in order to buy supplies for civilians suffering from sanctions applied after the invasion of Kuwait in 1990.
The original oil deal was agreed in May, 1996 but didn't commence until December 10 due to a series of delays, mainly because of questions raised by the U.S. about monitoring and other issues.

The deal was renewed last week by the U.N. Secuirty Council following a review of the first 180-day round and took effect June 8. But Hamdoon said the procedure for restarting oil liftings was on track.
The fact no oil sales contracts will be submitted for U.N. approval before a distribution plan is likely to mean no Iraqi liftings will take place in June, Hamdoon said.
A hiatus in crude liftings from Iraq was widely expected by oil traders.
"The pricing formula is needed for the new contracts. There will be no crude lifted until then," said Hamdoon.
The Iraqi envoy noted that he foresaw "no problem" in implementing a new distribution plan, saying no significant changes would be made to the food basket requests, and other plan specifics.
Hamdoon reiterated that oil companies holding term contracts with the Iraqi State Oil Marketing Organization (SOMO) would have their deals renewed under the second round of the oil sales accord.
